ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rhombus $ABCD$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$, and $OE \perp AB$ at point $E$. If $\angle ADC = 130^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle AOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In rhombus $ABCD$, $\angle ADC=130^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BAD=180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BAO= \frac{1}{2}\angle BAD= \frac{1}{2}\times50^\circ=25^\circ$, \\
$\because OE\perp AB$, \\
$\therefore \angle AOE=90^\circ-\angle BAO=90^\circ-25^\circ=\boxed{65^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a rhombus ABCD, with A on the left, B below, C on the right, and D above; diagonal AC horizontally connects A, O, C, and diagonal BD vertically connects D, O, B; the two diagonals intersect at O. Point E is on side AB, segment OE connects from O to AB, and there is a right-angle mark at E, indicating OE⊥AB. Then reason: It is known that ∠ADC=130°. A rhombus is a parallelogram, so adjacent interior angles are supplementary; therefore ∠BAD=180°−130°=50°. The diagonal AC of a rhombus bisects ∠BAD, and O is on AC, so ∠BAO=50°÷2=25°. Also because OE⊥AB, OE and AB form 90°. The angle between AO and AB is 25°, therefore the angle between AO and OE is ∠AOE=90°−25°=65°.
